doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: A recent Robby Krieger session in the key of E
summary: A recent Doors guitarist session reminds him jazz tunes are never in E.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well they’re certainly not as easy to do, you just reminded me, recently I did a session for Robby Krieger of the Doors. He’s still around. He’s got a beautiful recording studio in Glendale, and I was called. He wanted me to play on something. In the middle of this tune it was sort of like a tribute to Bill — I don’t know what the thing was, but anyway it was a jazz based lyric although it was a rock & roll tune for sure. But he said something about, “Well play ‘Remember Bird’” or something like that, and then there’s this section. And I’m supposed to — I have an alto saxophone and I’m supposed to play it. It’s of course, he’s a guitar player. What key do you think it’s in? E. And I got through it but I told him, “Robbie listen, if you ever write any tribute to jazz again don’t do it in E. Don’t do it ever.” If you go through the jazz fake books you won’t find one tune in the key of E. I guarantee it.
I’d like to talk about that later if we get back to it. But continue — so you go in the booth and Lou is there. Is Carole King there?
